statement: Kernel-checked; advisory statement coverage and independent review remain open. For either signed odd-return map S_s, every r>=1 and real table h modulo 3^r that is zero on multiples of three and positive on all unit residues has a unit class a modulo 3^(r+1), delta>0 and B>=1 such that every odd m>=B in class a satisfies m*W_h(m)<=h(m mod 3^r)-delta. Here W_h(m) is the full sum of h(n mod 3^r)/n over actual positive odd predecessors S_s(n)=m, without multiplicity. The positive odd unit targets with m*W_h(m)<h(m mod 3^r) have divergent reciprocal mass. For every E with finite sum_{m in E} 1/m, some such deficient target lies outside E. The final theorem states the actual predecessor sum explicitly. This is an ambient one-generation obstruction to uniform reproduction; it does not bound any fate class intersection or prove termination.

Kernel-checked; advisory statement coverage and independent review remain open. For either sign s in {1,-1}, let S_s(n)=(3n+s)/2^v2(3n+s) on positive odd integers. For every r>=0, real table 0<=h<=H modulo 3^r, and positive odd target m, the actual series W_h(m)=sum_{n>=1 odd, S_s(n)=m} h(n mod 3^r)/n converges and satisfies |m*W_h(m)-L_s h(m mod 3^(r+1))|<=H/(m-1/2), where L_s is the complete homogeneous odd-return operator. Every actual predecessor corresponds to exactly one admissible positive halving exponent. No vanishing on multiples of three or fate-distribution assumption is needed for this one-generation estimate. Actual errors at higher fixed depths are a separate written result.
